title: JavaScript and the DOM: Making Pages Interactive

questions.question: What does the defer attribute on a script tag do?
options: Blocks HTML parsing until the script has run
Downloads the script in parallel and executes it after parsing, in document order
Executes the script the moment its download finishes, in any order
Runs the script before the HTML is parsed
questions.rationale: defer downloads in parallel without blocking the parser, then runs after the document is parsed and in the order the tags appear — the modern default.

questions.question: What does document.querySelector("#todo li") return?
options: The first element matching that CSS selector, or null if none matches
An array of every matching element
An HTML string of the matches
It always returns all matches as a NodeList
questions.rationale: querySelector returns the first match only; querySelectorAll is the variant that returns every match as a NodeList.

questions.question: Which property is the safe choice for displaying user-provided text?
options: innerHTML
outerHTML
textContent
document.write
questions.rationale: textContent inserts plain text with no markup parsing, so injected HTML cannot execute; innerHTML and document.write parse the string and enable XSS.

questions.question: In what order do the phases of event propagation unfold for an ordinary click?
options: Bubbling first, then capture
Only the target's listeners run
A random order chosen per event
Capture travels down to the target, then the event bubbles back up to window
questions.rationale: The event descends during capture, fires at the target, then bubbles upward — and ordinary addEventListener handlers run in the bubble phase.

questions.question: What is the main benefit of event delegation?
options: It makes CSS selectors faster
One listener on an ancestor covers present and future children via bubbling
It automatically prevents all default browser actions
It removes the need for the DOM entirely
questions.rationale: Because events bubble, a single parent listener can inspect event.target and serve every descendant, including elements added after binding.

questions.question: Inside an event handler, what is the difference between event.target and event.currentTarget?
options: target is where the event originated; currentTarget is the element the listener is attached to
They are always the same element
currentTarget is always the clicked text node
target exists only during the capture phase
questions.rationale: In delegated handlers the listener sits on the ancestor (currentTarget) while the click may land on a deep child (target), which is why handlers use target.closest(selector).

questions.question: A fetch request receives a 404 response. What happens?
options: The promise rejects and the catch block runs
The browser navigates to its error page
The promise resolves; you must check response.ok to detect the failure
response.json() throws a SyntaxError
questions.rationale: fetch only rejects on network-level failures; HTTP error statuses still resolve, so handlers must verify response.ok or response.status themselves.

questions.question: What does await actually do inside an async function?
options: It starts a new background thread
It freezes the entire browser main thread
It cancels the promise if it takes too long
It pauses this async function until the promise settles, letting other events run meanwhile
questions.rationale: await suspends only the async function, not the page: the single-threaded event loop keeps processing clicks and rendering until the result arrives.

questions.question: What is layout thrashing?
options: Writing too many CSS classes in one stylesheet
Interleaving DOM reads and writes, forcing the browser into repeated reflows
Using querySelector too many times on one page
Attaching too many listeners to a single element
questions.rationale: Each measurement after a style write invalidates layout and forces a synchronous reflow; batching reads and writes (or animating transform and opacity) avoids it.

questions.question: Which practice makes animations smooth instead of triggering constant layout work?
options: Animating the top and left properties
Driving frames with setInterval
Animating only transform and opacity, which skip layout
Raising the element's z-index
questions.rationale: transform and opacity are handled by the compositor without re-running layout or paint, so they animate cheaply even on slow devices.
